Taking care of the soil

Simple techniques
Respecting our environment

Bio-intensive market gardening on living soil allows for increased production while building, season after season, a more fertile, more living, and more structured soil.

This method relies on simple, reproducible agricultural techniques that respect both health and the environment.

pages.title: LIVING SOIL
pages.text:
BIO-INTENSIVE

The method is based on two main pillars:

- **Living soil**: regenerating the biological life of the soil to naturally nourish plants.

- **Bio-intensive**: producing more with less, by optimizing space and resources.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour SOL VIVANT

pages.title: Living Soil
pages.text:
Living soil is soil that contains life: earthworms, insects, bacteria, fungi...

Together, they transform and improve the soil, allowing it to naturally nourish and strengthen plants.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Le sol vivant

pages.title: Living Soil
pages.text:
We build living soil through simple but effective practices:

1. Establishing permanent, no-till raised beds,
2. Gentle irrigation across the entire plot,
3. Active compost in the pathways.

For the method to work long-term, certain practices are essential:

1. Permanent growing beds,
2. Well-defined and mulched pathways,
3. Always available compost,
4. Watering of the beds and also the pathways.
4. Irrigation

pages.title: WALKWAYS
pages.text:
BEDS The method consists of working on permanent cultivation beds that are fixed and well-defined.

Between the beds, there are walkways for circulation.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour PASSE-PIEDS

pages.title: Time and Energy Savings
pages.text:
Less erosion and leaching
Concentrated fertile soil
Less compacted soil
Suitable for small spaces

Permanent raised beds offer many advantages:

- Fertile soil is concentrated where plants grow.
- The soil is less compacted.
- The soil is protected against erosion and leaching.
- Time and energy savings.
- The method is suitable for small spaces.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Gain de temps et énergie

pages.title: 2. The Benefit of Walkways
pages.text: 2. The Benefit of Walkways
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour 2. L’intérêt des passe-pieds

pages.title: In this market gardening method, pathways are not just for circulation.
pages.text:
They are active areas:

- Compost is passively made there through the decomposition of mulch.

- They also help maintain humidity.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Dans cette méthode de maraîchage, les passe-pieds ne servent pas seulement à circuler.

pages.title: 3. Ensuring Compost Availability
pages.text: 3. Ensuring Compost Availability
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour 3. Assurer la disponibilité du compost

pages.title: COMPOST
pages.text:
Compost formed in the walkways is moved to the cultivation beds to help soil life establish itself more quickly.

But this production is not always sufficient.

It is therefore important to supplement it with other organic matter inputs.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour COMPOST

pages.title: To remain self-sufficient, one solution is to make your own compost.
pages.text: The winter composting system allows for the valorization of materials available during the rainy season to produce quality compost at a lower cost.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Pour rester autonome, une des solutions est de fabriquer soi-même son compost.

pages.title: Winter composting in a compost bin is an effective method. Other techniques include:
pages.text:
- **Compost pit**: a simple option when construction materials are scarce
- **Compost pile**: directly on the ground, covered to retain moisture
- **Bokashi method**: rapid fermentation of kitchen waste, even in small quantities
- **Surface compost**: directly depositing materials on beds to slowly nourish the soil

pages.title: 4. Principle of Gentle and Holistic Irrigation
pages.text: 4. Principle of Gentle and Holistic Irrigation
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour 4. Principe d'une irrigation douce et globale

pages.title: In this method, the entire plot is irrigated, including the pathways. The global watering method
pages.text:
by sprinkling can be done mechanically, with sprinkler heads, or manually with a simple watering can.

The goal is not only to water the plants but to maintain soil moisture.

We aim to mimic the effect of regular, gentle rain, which nourishes soil life without disturbing it.

pages.text:

But bio-intensive market gardening on living soil also covers the following topics:

- Direct sowing and transplanting.

- Nursery and young plant production.

- Crop planning and rotation.

- Harvesting, storage, and valorization of produce.

- Use of adapted seeds.

- Ecological crop protection.

pages.title: Bio-intensive market gardening in living soil is a way of cultivating in connection with the soil: a soil that we nourish, that
pages.text:
improves, and that gives back to us.

This approach allows us to:

- Produce more by cultivating more efficiently
- Be autonomous in the production of our inputs
- Work with simple and accessible tools
- Reproduce, evolve, and transmit sustainable practices
